entities.name: Cem Sultan
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cem Sultan (1459–1495) was an Ottoman prince, son of Mehmed II, who contested the succession with his brother Bayezid II after 1481 and spent his remaining years as a high-value exile in Europe. Defeated in Anatolian civil war, he fled to the Mamluks and then into Christian custody—Rhodes, France, and the Papacy—where rulers used him as leverage against Istanbul.

Cem’s captivity became a diplomatic commodity: European courts threatened to unleash an alternative Ottoman claimant while Bayezid paid to keep him contained. He died in Naples in 1495, still a pawn of Mediterranean great-power rivalry.

His career dramatises Ottoman succession violence and the entanglement of Islamic and Christian diplomacy in the late fifteenth century.
